title: Sharabhanga
hook: an old man lights a fire and steps into it, and then the other sages show Rama what they've been hiding

segments.voice: Yesterday: your line, I'll earn my own worlds. Sharabhanga offered Rama all his merit, and Rama kindly said no.

Sharabhanga asks Rama to wait and watch. He builds a fire, makes the offering of clarified butter, and with the words of the rite, steps into the flames. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stand there. The old body burns away. And out of the fire, Valmiki says, rises a young man, shining, who goes up to the world of Brahma. The sage had waited only for this: to see his guest, and then to go.
screen: `WAIT AND WATCH.` → `HE STEPS INTO THE FIRE.` → `A YOUNG MAN RISES.`

segments.voice: It's important to say what this scene is and isn't. Sharabhanga is a great ascetic at the very end of a long life of tapas, already invited to heaven by Indra himself. His entry into the fire is presented as a sacred departure, a completed life, not a despairing one, and the text treats it with awe. Then the mood changes. Word has spread that Rama is here, and the sages gather around him, many kinds of ascetics, Valmiki says, some living on water alone, some on air, some standing in rivers. They lead him to a place in the forest where bones are piled up: the bodies of sages killed by rakshasas, the man-eating demons who roam Dandaka. Look, they say. This is what happens to us. They're slaughtering us, and we have no protector. You are our refuge. Remember the sages' first request: be our king, protect us. Now Rama sees why. Not a vague danger, but this. And he answers directly. I came to this forest to keep my father's word, but I'll do this too. I'll destroy the rakshasas who harm you. That promise matters. It's freely made, by a man under no orders, in front of witnesses. And in the chapters ahead it will be tested, and questioned, by someone very close to him.
screen: `A SACRED DEPARTURE, NOT DESPAIR.` · `THE SAGES GATHER.` · `A PILE OF BONES IN THE FOREST.` · `RAMA'S PROMISE.` · then, large: `I'LL PROTECT YOU.`

segments.voice: Think of something you've seen recently that wasn't right, something real, not abstract, and look at it honestly for a moment, the way Rama looked at what the sages showed him, without flooding yourself. Then ask quietly whether one small thing is within your reach, and let the answer come, or not.
Sharabhanga. The old sage who rose from the fire to Brahma's world. After him, the sages show Rama the bones, and Rama promises to protect them.
Your line: I'll protect you. No one ordered Rama to say it. That's day five hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Ramayana reciters tell Sharabhanga's departure with reverence, and Rama's promise to the sages here sets up the battles later in the Aranya Kanda.

original.note: Sanskrit agni: fire, and the god of fire, who carries offerings up to the gods.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sage dies in a fire.
what it means: a great ascetic completes his life, rising from the fire to Brahma's world.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 5 ends with the departure; Aranya 6 brings the bones and Rama's vow, which frames the conflicts of the forest book.

chat.says: Why did the sages show Rama a pile of bones in the forest?
options: Rakshasas were killing them, and they had no protector, so they asked Rama.
It was an old burial ground, and they wanted Rama to bless it.
They wanted to warn Rama to leave the forest before it was too late.
chat.meaning: The bones were sages killed by rakshasas. Having no protector, the sages asked Rama for refuge, and he promised to destroy those who harmed them.

Sharabhanga.meaning: an old sage of Dandaka who waited to see Rama

Brahma.meaning: the creator god; his world is a high heaven

Dandaka.meaning: the great wild forest of the south in the Ramayana
